correctness.rationale: Reconstruction from the death–birth transition rates gives \(\dot x=(N_1/D_1-x)/2\), \(\dot y=(N_2/D_2-y)/2\). The exact polynomial sum \(P+Q=(x-y)[1-(1-m)(x+y)]\) forces \(X+Y=1/(1-m)\) on the analytic near-\((1,0)\) equilibrium branch. The frozen Jacobian is exactly diagonal with entries \(-1/6,-1/4\) at zero migration; continuity yields a uniformly contracting invariant rectangle for small nonnegative migration. The period map gives a unique local periodic orbit. Uniform tracking of the moving equilibrium has error \(O(q/T)\), and \(\int_0^\pi d\theta/(1-q\cos^2\theta)=\pi/\sqrt{1-q}\) yields the exact adiabatic mean. The inequalities follow from \((1-q/2)^2-(1-q)=q^2/4>0\). Exact symbolic and illustrative numerical checks were executed from the bundled verification code; the proof does not rely on finite sampling. No finite-population statement is asserted.

value.rationale: The motivating population-genetic study explicitly seeks the effect of a varying migration schedule at fixed migration mean. The exact frozen equilibrium identity makes the nonlinear adiabatic average computable in closed form, yielding a strict \(q^2/16\) seasonal enhancement relative to constant *mean* migration while remaining below constant *peak* migration. This distinguishes empirically and conceptually different baselines and supplies a motivated, sharp-sign mathematical boundary to a claimed contraction pattern, beyond mere numerical repetition. The value does not depend on a downstream general theorem or empirical ecological validation.
